# Authorization & Write Boundary Checklist: Issues — creation, detail and editing

**Purpose**: Validate that the authorization requirements in `spec.md` are complete, unambiguous, mutually consistent and objectively verifiable, before the feature is decomposed into tasks
**Created**: 2026-08-31
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [contracts/mutators.md](../contracts/mutators.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

This is a **requirements-quality** review, not a verification pass. Every item asks whether something is *written well*, not whether code *works*.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is the predicate for every mutator this feature delivers stated, with no mutator left to inherit its predicate from §2 by implication? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK002 Are requirements defined for the case where a mutator is called against an issue that does not exist — and is it specified whether the caller learns "not found" or "forbidden" first? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK003 Is it specified whether the server must validate that a submitted assignee belongs to the pool `FR-022` defines, or whether the pool is a UI affordance only? [Gap, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK004 Are requirements defined for a caller whose account is deactivated mid-session but whose session token is still valid? [Gap, Assumption]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the content of the inline reason specified beyond "names the project" — enough that two implementers would write the same sentence? [Completeness, Spec §FR-023, §FR-026]
- [ ] CHK006 Are requirements stated for whether these mutators are subject to any rate limiting or abuse control, or is their exclusion deliberate? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the `isMember` predicate's admin-implicit behaviour restated where this feature relies on it, rather than only cited? [Completeness, Spec §FR-022, US4 scenario 6]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK008 Is "on the next render" quantified — does a client-side navigation, a revalidation, or only a full page load satisfy it? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK009 Is "derive the project it checks from the stored row" unambiguous for `createIssue`, which has no stored issue row to derive from? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK010 Is "every route including one that bypasses a disabled control" specific enough to enumerate the routes a reviewer must consider? [Clarity, Spec §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the distinction between a membership *predicate* and a membership *list* stated where this feature uses both, rather than left to §2? [Clarity, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK012 Can "the page explains why and names the project they would need to be added to" be objectively evaluated, or does it admit several materially different pages? [Measurability, Spec §FR-023]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK013 Do the read-access requirements agree across every statement of them — no requirement in this feature makes membership a visibility boundary anywhere? [Consistency, Spec §FR-021, §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK014 Are the disabled-control requirements consistent between the rail, the title and description, the header's New issue control and the Delete control? [Consistency, Spec §FR-026, §FR-028, §FR-054, §FR-061]
- [ ] CHK015 Do the requirements for the create route's refusal and the create control's disabled state remain independent everywhere both are mentioned, with neither implying the other was applied? [Consistency, Spec §FR-029]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the hide-versus-disable rule applied consistently — is it stated that nothing on either screen is hidden for a permission reason, and that §2's hiding exception covers admin-only navigation only? [Consistency, Spec §FR-047, §SC-012]
- [ ] CHK017 Do `FR-018`'s predicate assignments agree with §2's write-rules list for all three mutators, with no fourth mutator implied by either? [Consistency, Spec §FR-018]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK018 Is there a measurable success criterion for the assigned-non-member state, and does it state what the user must be able to read rather than what the system must render? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-008]
- [ ] CHK019 Can "the server refuses it" be objectively verified for each of the three mutators without reference to an implementation? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007, §SC-010]
- [ ] CHK020 Are the acceptance scenarios for User Story 4 sufficient to cover every user class the matrix in §2 distinguishes — admin, member, non-member, assigned non-member, unauthenticated? [Coverage, Spec §US4]

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK021 Are requirements defined for an admin who holds no membership row, on every surface this feature delivers rather than only on the issue page? [Coverage, Spec §US4 scenario 6]
- [ ] CHK022 Are requirements defined for the transition where membership is granted mid-session — the mirror of `FR-025`'s removal case? [Gap, Spec §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK023 Are requirements defined for an unauthenticated caller reaching each of the three mutators directly, distinct from reaching the two routes? [Gap, Spec §FR-029]
- [ ] CHK024 Is it specified whether a member may assign an issue to a user who has since been removed from the project — as opposed to keeping an existing such assignment? [Gap, Spec §FR-024]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK025 Is the dependency on R5's `isMember` predicate stated as a contract this feature consumes, including what it must return for an admin with no row? [Dependency, Spec §Dependencies]
- [ ] CHK026 Is the assumption that every signed-in caller has already been resolved to an actor by R1 stated where these mutators rely on it? [Assumption]
- [ ] CHK027 Is the obligation R11 places on these mutators — recipient computation gated on a changed, non-cleared assignee — stated precisely enough that R11's author need not re-derive it? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- An unchecked item is a question for the spec, not a defect in the plan — several of these are already answered in [contracts/mutators.md](../contracts/mutators.md), which is precisely the finding: the requirement lives in the plan rather than the spec
